summary: This room is the palace's infrastructure-and-self-description belt (STIGMERGY, SUBSTRATE, ROSETTA, Project Stewardship System, Swarm Weave, Symbiotic Skills, The Scroll, The Palace Voice, plus the conatus/threshold philosophy cluster and a handful of small design-discipline seeds). It reads coherent — the machinery genuinely does serve the values it claims to, and two entries (Progressive Staging vs. Symbiotic Skills) turn out to be arguing with each other about whether staged design generalizes to organic growth without ever having met. The clearest de-sprawl move is confirming a compost already in motion (Tristitia Generator, nutrients already in Spinoza Conatus) and merging a self-aware seed (Two Batons, One Board, whose own forward vector asks to dissolve into Project Stewardship System) into the entry that already treats it as one case. Two small design-discipline entries (Speak Like a Person Log Like a Protocol, The Reader's Context Window) are the palace's actual UI philosophy but sit unlinked from The Palace Voice, the entry that should be their parent. And ROSETTA and Self-Describing Knowledge Module — both meta-pages about what the palace *is* — disagree with each other on four points, which they both partially know (SDKM names it as an open question) but neither has fixed.

typed_relations.source: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol
typed_relations.rationale: SLPLP is a concrete, dated instance of the general voice discipline (translate jargon, protect the reader from the wire) applied to one surface (STIGMERGY). Palace Voice's Registers section discusses mode-riding registers but never names SLPLP as its own worked example, though SLPLP predates it by a month.
typed_relations.evidence: "Two registers, always co-present, never confused" (SLPLP) vs Palace Voice's "Jargon → off. Translate or gloss."

typed_relations.label: order-and-word
typed_relations.rationale: Reader's Context Window already names itself "the structural sibling of Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol" — words vs. order. The Palace Voice is the words-discipline for the whole palace; Reader's Context Window is the missing order-discipline. Neither points at the other.
typed_relations.evidence: "That principle governs the register of the words on a surface; this one governs their sequence and their count. Together they are the two laws of a palace front-end."

typed_relations.label: staged-complexity
typed_relations.rationale: Both name the same pattern — commit to a tier/stage only after it proves itself, each stage/tier complete and usable on its own, never retroactive — from opposite folders (Shop dispatch vocabulary vs. instrument-design method) and never cite each other.
typed_relations.evidence: "Sketch is calibration... Study is the working draft... Piece is the deliverable" (Tier Vocabulary Glossary) vs "every stage is a complete, playable, useful artifact... Additive complexity, never retroactive" (Progressive Staging)

typed_relations.label: staged-design-vs-organic-growth
typed_relations.rationale: Progressive Staging is the palace's confident method for staged design (works when 'the domain has natural layers of complexity'). Symbiotic Skills' own six-week archaeology found the palace's actual growth did the opposite of staged: commit 1 was already 27 dense files, the predicted Node→Edge→Typed Edge sequence never happened observably, and growth was six *overlapping* stages, not additive ones. Productive tension: does progressive staging generalize past engineered artifacts to knowledge-organism growth, or is organic growth structurally exempt from it?
typed_relations.evidence: Progressive Staging: "It doesn't work when the domain is irreducibly complex." Symbiotic Skills: "The palace did not start as a node... The Node → Edge → Typed Edge → Network developmental stages happened, but they happened off-camera."

coherence_findings.issue: Two of the palace's own self-description tables disagree with each other on four points: (1) whether the palace is a 'module / runtime' (SDKM) or 'a system of modules / a runtime' (ROSETTA); (2) SDKM has no row for the Ceremony Contract, only the Ceremony Linter; (3) a ceremony is a read-only SPARQL query in SDKM's table but a query-plus-update in ROSETTA's; (4) SDKM collapses Entry Type and SCHEMA.md into one row where ROSETTA splits them with different DDD terms. SDKM already names all four discrepancies in its own Open Questions and calls resolving them 'prior to Proof 1, not parallel to it.'
coherence_findings.proposed_action: A short reconciliation pass, owned by whichever page becomes authoritative (SDKM's own suggestion is that this matters more than it looks, since transfer — Proof 1/2/3 — depends on which table is right). Not urgent, but it's a self-description entry disagreeing with itself across two canon pages, which is the exact class of thing this Weave's community lens exists to catch.

synthesis_spawn_flag.unnamed_idea: Stage as a universal palace primitive — the same 'commit to the next level of fidelity only once the current one is proven' logic appears as an entry's SCHEMA `stage` field, Progressive Staging's design method, Tier Vocabulary Glossary's Sketch/Study/Piece, and Project Stewardship System's stage-conditional steward posture.
synthesis_spawn_flag.why_load_bearing: If this pattern is real it explains why so many unrelated palace subsystems independently reinvented the same staged-commitment logic — but it may already be adequately covered by Substrate Skill § Stage as Alignment Confidence, which this room did not have as a member. Recommend a worker who has read Substrate Skill confirm before spawning a new entry — this may be redundant rather than missing.
